title.zh: 卷九十一 晉書17: 列傳六 房知溫 王建立 康福 安彥威 李周 張從訓 李繼忠 李頃 周光輔 符彥饒 羅周敬 鄭琮
title.en: Volume 91 Book of Later Jin 17: Biographies 6 - Fang Zhiwen, Wang Jianli, Kang Fu, An Yanwei, Li Zhou, Zhang Congxun, Li Jizhong, Li Qing, Zhou Guangfu, Fu Yanrao, Luo Zhoujing, Zheng Cong
title.raw: 卷九十一 晉書17: 列傳六 房知溫 王建立 康福 安彥威 李周 張從訓 李繼忠 李頃 周光輔 符彥饒 羅周敬 鄭琮 Volume 91 Book of Later Jin 17: Biographies 6 - Fang Zhiwen, Wang Jianli, Kang Fu, An Yanwei, Li Zhou, Zhang Congxun, Li Jizhong, Li Qing, Zhou Guangfu, Fu Yanrao, Luo Zhoujing, Zheng Cong

sentences.zh: 房知溫，字伯玉，兗州瑕丘人也。

translations.literal: Fang Zhiwen, style name Boyu, was a man of Xiqiu in Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Zhiwen, whose courtesy name was Boyu, came from Xiqiu in Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 少有勇力，籍名於本軍，為赤甲都官健。

translations.literal: In youth he had courage and strength; his name was registered in his home army, and he served as a red-armor company officer's guard.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he was strong and bold; registered with his home garrison, he served as a guardsman in the red-armor command.

sentences.zh: （《玉堂閑話》：知溫少年，與外弟徐某為盜於兗、鄆之境。）〉

translations.literal: (From the 《Yutang Xianhua》: In his youth Zhiwen and a maternal cousin surnamed Xu were bandits in the borderlands of Yan and Yun.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (According to the 《Yutang Xianhua》, in his youth Zhiwen and a cousin on his mother's side, one Xu, had been bandits along the Yan–Yun border.)〉

sentences.zh: 梁將葛從周鎮其地，選置麾下。

translations.literal: The Liang general Ge Congzhou was stationed in that region and selected him for placement under his command.
translations.idiomatic: When the Later Liang general Ge Congzhou held that territory, he took Zhiwen onto his staff.

sentences.zh: 時部將牛存節屯於鎮，好摴博，每求辨采者，知溫以善博見推，因得侍左右，遂熟於存節。

translations.literal: At the time the subordinate general Niu Cunjie was garrisoned at the post and loved to play dice; whenever he sought someone to judge the stakes, Zhiwen was recommended for skill at gambling and thus attended at his side, becoming familiar with Cunjie.
translations.idiomatic: The division commander Niu Cunjie was then stationed there and was fond of dice; whenever he needed someone to settle wagers, Zhiwen was recommended for his skill at gambling, gained a place at Cunjie's side, and came to know him well.

sentences.zh: 及王師範遣劉鄩據兗州，梁祖命存節將兵討之，知溫夕縋出奔，存節喜而納焉。

translations.literal: When Wang Shifan sent Liu Yan to hold Yanzhou, the Liang founder ordered Cunjie to lead troops against him; Zhiwen was let down by rope at night and fled out, and Cunjie gladly received him.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Shifan sent Liu Yan to seize Yanzhou, the Liang founder ordered Cunjie to attack him; Zhiwen slipped out of the city by rope one night and fled to Cunjie, who welcomed him gladly.

sentences.zh: 明夜，竊良馬一駟，復入城，鄩乃擢為裨將。

translations.literal: The next night he stole a team of fine horses and re-entered the city; Yan then promoted him to deputy commander.
translations.idiomatic: The following night he stole a team of good horses and rode back into the city, and Yan promoted him to deputy commander.

sentences.zh: 鄩降，隸於同州劉知俊，知俊補為克和軍使。

translations.literal: When Yan surrendered, Zhiwen was attached to Liu Zhijun of Tongzhou; Zhijun appointed him commander of the Kehe Army.
translations.idiomatic: After Yan surrendered, Zhiwen entered the service of Liu Zhijun in Tongzhou, who made him commander of the Kehe Army.

sentences.zh: 知俊奔岐，改隸魏州楊師厚，以為馬步軍校，漸升至親隨指揮使，繼加檢校司空。

translations.literal: When Zhijun fled to Qi, Zhiwen was reassigned to Yang Shihou of Weizhou as cavalry-and-infantry corps officer, gradually rising to personal escort commander, and was later given the honorary title of Acting Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhijun fled to Qi, Zhiwen transferred to Yang Shihou in Weizhou as a cavalry-and-infantry officer, rose step by step to personal escort commander, and was later given the honorary rank of Acting Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 莊宗入魏，賜姓，名紹英，改天雄軍馬步都指揮使，加檢校司徒、澶州刺史、行臺右千牛衛大將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuangzong entered Wei, he was granted the imperial surname and the name Shaoying, made overall cavalry-and-infantry commander of the Tianxiong Army, and further given Acting Minister over the Masses, prefect of Chanzhou, and Grand General of the Right Thousand-Ox Guard of the field headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuangzong entered Wei, he was granted the imperial surname Li and the name Shaoying, appointed overall cavalry-and-infantry commander of the Tianxiong Army, and given the additional titles of Acting Minister over the Masses, prefect of Chanzhou, and Grand General of the Right Thousand-Ox Guard on the field staff.

sentences.zh: 莊宗平梁，歷曹、貝州刺史，權充東北面蕃漢馬步都虞候，遣戍瓦橋關。

translations.literal: After Zhuangzong pacified Liang, he served successively as prefect of Cao and Bei prefectures, acted as overall tribal-and-Han cavalry-and-infantry deputy commander for the northeast, and was sent to garrison Waqiao Pass.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhuangzong conquered the Liang, he served as prefect of Cao and then Bei, acted as overall deputy commander of tribal and Han cavalry and infantry in the northeast, and was posted to garrison Waqiao Pass.

sentences.zh: 明宗自鄴入洛，知溫與王晏球首赴焉。

translations.literal: When Emperor Mingzong entered Luoyang from Ye, Zhiwen and Wang Yanqiu were the first to go to meet him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Mingzong marched from Ye into Luoyang, Zhiwen and Wang Yanqiu were the first to come out to join him.

sentences.zh: 明宗自總管府署知溫滑州兩使留後。

translations.literal: From the chief administrator's office Mingzong appointed Zhiwen acting military governor of both circuits in Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: From his headquarters as chief administrator, Mingzong appointed Zhiwen acting military governor of Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 天成元年，授兗州節度使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tiancheng he was made military governor of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tiancheng (926) he was appointed military governor of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 明宗即位，詔充北面招討，屯於盧臺軍。

translations.literal: When Mingzong took the throne, an edict appointed him northern campaign commander, and he encamped at the Lutai garrison.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong ascended the throne, he was ordered to serve as northern campaign commander and encamped at the Lutai garrison.

sentences.zh: 以盧文進來歸，加特進、同平章事，賞招討之功也。

translations.literal: Because Lu Wenjin came over in surrender, he was given the special advancement rank and made co–Grand Councillor, as a reward for his campaign achievements.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Wenjin defected to the court, Zhiwen was given the rank of Special Advancement and made co–Grand Councillor in reward for his campaign service.

sentences.zh: 後除烏震為招討副使，代知溫歸鎮。

translations.literal: Later Wu Zhen was removed and made deputy campaign commander in Zhiwen's place, and Zhiwen returned to his post.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zhen was later appointed deputy campaign commander to replace Zhiwen, who returned to his governorship.

sentences.zh: 知溫怒震遽至，有怨言，因縱博，誘牙兵殺震於席上。

translations.literal: Zhiwen was angry that Zhen had arrived so abruptly and nursed complaints; he therefore set up gambling, lured the guard troops, and had Zhen killed at the gaming table.
translations.idiomatic: Angry that Zhen had arrived so suddenly and resentful of the slight, Zhiwen staged a gambling session, incited his guard troops, and had Zhen killed at the table.

sentences.zh: 會次將安審通保騎軍隔河按甲不動，知溫懼不濟，乃束身渡水，復結審通，逐其亂軍以奏。

translations.literal: The deputy commander An Shentong held the cavalry across the river with arms at rest and did not move; fearing failure, Zhiwen bound himself and crossed the water, renewed ties with Shentong, drove off the mutinous troops, and reported it.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy commander An Shentong held the cavalry on the far bank without moving; fearing the plot would fail, Zhiwen went over in person, won Shentong back to his side, drove off the mutinous troops, and reported the affair to the court.

sentences.zh: 時朝廷姑息知溫，下詔於鄴盡殺軍士家口老幼凡數萬，清漳為之變色。

translations.literal: At the time the court indulged Zhiwen; an edict at Ye ordered the slaughter of all dependents of the soldiers, old and young, numbering tens of thousands, and the Qingzhang River ran red.
translations.idiomatic: The court indulged Zhiwen; an edict at Ye ordered the massacre of tens of thousands of soldiers' dependents, young and old alike, and the Qingzhang River turned red with blood.

sentences.zh: 尋詔遣知溫就便之鎮，以安反側。

translations.literal: Soon an edict sent Zhiwen back to his post at convenience, to pacify those inclined to revolt.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was ordered back to his governorship to calm the unrest.

sentences.zh: 俄改徐州節度使，加兼侍中。

translations.literal: Shortly he was changed to military governor of Xuzhou and given the additional title of Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to military governor of Xuzhou and given the additional title of Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 會朝廷起兵伐高季興，授荊南招討使，知行府事。

translations.literal: When the court raised troops against Gao Jixing, he was made campaign commander for Jingnan and acted as administrator of the campaign headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: When the court marched against Gao Jixing, he was appointed campaign commander for Jingnan and placed in charge of the campaign headquarters.

sentences.zh: 尋丁母憂，起復雲麾將軍，墨缞即戎，竟無功而還。

translations.literal: Soon he entered mourning for his mother; recalled from mourning as Cloud-Banner General, he took the field in unbleached hemp and in the end returned without achievement.
translations.idiomatic: He soon went into mourning for his mother; recalled as Cloud-Banner General, he took the field still in mourning garb and ultimately returned without success.

sentences.zh: 長興中，節制文陽。

translations.literal: In the Changxing era he controlled Wenyang.
translations.idiomatic: During the Changxing period (930–933) he held command over Wenyang.

sentences.zh: 越二年，除平盧軍節度使，累官至開府儀同三司、檢校太師、兼中書令，封東平王，食邑五千戶，食實封三百戶。

translations.literal: Two years later he was made military governor of the Pinglu Army, rose in office to Grand Preceptor of the Palace with the same ceremonial rank as the Three Excellencies, Acting Grand Preceptor, and concurrent Director of the Secretariat, was enfeoffed as Prince of Dongping with a fief of five thousand households and three hundred actual enfeoffed households.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later he was appointed military governor of the Pinglu Army, rose to Grand Preceptor of the Palace with ceremonial parity with the Three Excellencies, Acting Grand Preceptor, and concurrent Director of the Secretariat, and was enfeoffed as Prince of Dongping with a nominal fief of five thousand households and three hundred actual enfeoffed households.

sentences.zh: 天福元年冬十二月辛巳，卒於鎮。

translations.literal: On the xinsi day of the twelfth month of winter in the first year of Tianfu, he died at his post.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinsi day of the twelfth month of winter in the first year of Tianfu (936), he died in office.

sentences.zh: 贈太尉，歸葬於瑕丘，詔立神道碑。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Grand Commandant, buried at Xiqiu, and an edict ordered a spirit-way stele erected.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Grand Commandant, buried at Xiqiu, and the court ordered a spirit-way stele erected for him.

sentences.zh: 知溫性粗獷，動罕由禮。

translations.literal: Zhiwen's nature was coarse and uncouth; his actions rarely followed ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiwen was coarse by nature and rarely acted with propriety.

sentences.zh: 每迎待王人，不改戎服，寡言笑，多縱左右排辱賓僚，他日知誤，亦無愧色。

translations.literal: Whenever he received imperial envoys he did not change out of military dress, spoke little and laughed little, and often let his attendants insult and humiliate his staff; when he later knew he had been wrong, he still showed no shame.
translations.idiomatic: When receiving imperial envoys he never changed out of his military dress, spoke little, and often allowed his attendants to bully and humiliate his staff; even when he later realized he had been in the wrong, he showed no shame.

sentences.zh: 始與唐末帝嘗失意於杯盤間，以白刃相恐，及末帝即位，知溫憂甚，末帝乃封王爵以寧之也。

translations.literal: He had once fallen out with the Last Tang Emperor over cups and dishes and threatened each other with bare blades; when the Last Emperor took the throne Zhiwen was deeply anxious, and the Last Emperor enfeoffed him as prince to reassure him.
translations.idiomatic: He had once quarreled with the Last Tang Emperor over wine and had threatened each other with drawn swords; when that emperor took the throne Zhiwen was deeply afraid, and the emperor enfeoffed him as prince to put his mind at ease.

sentences.zh: 知溫徑赴洛陽，申其宿過，且感新恩，末帝開懷以厚禮慰而遣之。

translations.literal: Zhiwen went straight to Luoyang, confessed his old fault, and expressed gratitude for the new favor; the Last Emperor opened his heart, comforted him with generous rites, and sent him away.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiwen went directly to Luoyang, confessed his old offense, and expressed gratitude for the new favor; the Last Emperor received him warmly, treated him generously, and sent him home reassured.

sentences.zh: 及還郡，厚斂不已，積貨數百萬，治第於南城，出則以妓樂相隨，任意所之，曾不以政事為務。

translations.literal: When he returned to his command he levied heavily without cease, amassed goods worth millions, built a mansion in the southern city, and whenever he went out was followed by singing girls and musicians, going wherever he pleased and never making governance his business.
translations.idiomatic: Back in his province he taxed relentlessly, amassed wealth in the millions, built a mansion in the southern quarter of the city, and whenever he went abroad was accompanied by musicians and courtesans, roaming as he pleased and paying no attention to government.

sentences.zh: 有幕客顏衎者，正直之士也，委曲陳其利病，知溫不能用焉。

translations.literal: Among his staff was a retainer named Yan Kan, an upright man who tactfully set forth the advantages and harms, but Zhiwen could not employ his counsel.
translations.idiomatic: His staff included Yan Kan, an upright man who tactfully explained what would help and what would harm him, but Zhiwen would not heed him.

sentences.zh: 及高祖建義入洛，尚不即進獻，耀兵於牙帳之下，衎正色謂曰：「清泰富有天下，多力善戰，豈明公之比！

translations.literal: When the High Ancestor raised righteous arms and entered Luoyang, Zhiwen still did not promptly submit tribute but displayed troops beneath his headquarters gate; Kan said sternly to him: "Qingtai possessed the realm and was strong in force and skilled in war—how could he be your equal!
translations.idiomatic: When the High Ancestor marched into Luoyang on his righteous campaign, Zhiwen still delayed submitting tribute and paraded his troops before headquarters; Kan said sternly to him: "Qingtai held the whole realm, was powerful, and fought well—how could you compare with him!

sentences.zh: 而天運有歸，坐成灰燼。

translations.literal: Yet when Heaven's mandate had its destination, he sat and became ashes.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when Heaven's mandate shifted, he was reduced to ashes in his seat.

sentences.zh: 今青州遷延不貢，何以求安？

translations.literal: Now Qingzhou delays and does not offer tribute—how can you seek safety?
translations.idiomatic: If Qingzhou now delays tribute, how can you hope for safety?

sentences.zh: 千百武夫，無足為恃，深為大王之所憂也。」

translations.literal: A thousand or ten thousand fighting men are not worth relying on—this is what Your Highness should deeply worry about."
translations.idiomatic: A few thousand soldiers are no real security—this is what ought to trouble you deeply, my lord."

sentences.zh: 知溫遂馳表稱賀，青人乃安。

translations.literal: Zhiwen then sent a swift memorial of congratulation, and the people of Qing were thereby reassured.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiwen then sent a hasty memorial of congratulation, and the people of Qingzhou were reassured.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以沈湎成疾而卒，部曲將吏分其所聚，例為富室。

translations.literal: Before long he died of illness brought on by dissipation; his officers and clerks divided what he had amassed and in every case became wealthy households.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died of illness brought on by debauchery; his officers and staff divided his hoarded wealth and in every case became rich men.

sentences.zh: 衎又勸其子彥儒進錢十萬貫，以助國用，朝廷除彥儒為沂州刺史。

translations.literal: Kan again urged his son Yanru to present one hundred thousand strings of cash to aid state expenses; the court appointed Yanru prefect of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Kan also urged his son Yanru to present one hundred thousand strings of cash to aid the treasury; the court appointed Yanru prefect of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 其家幸獲保全，皆衎之力也。

translations.literal: His family fortunately escaped destruction—all through Kan's efforts.
translations.idiomatic: His family was fortunate to escape ruin—entirely thanks to Kan.

sentences.zh: 王建立，遼州榆社人也。

translations.literal: Wang Jianli was a man of Yushe in Liaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jianli came from Yushe in Liaozhou.

sentences.zh: 曾祖秋，祖嘉，父弁，累贈太保。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather was Qiu, his grandfather Jia, his father Bian—all posthumously honored as Grand Guardian in succession.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather was Qiu, his grandfather Jia, and his father Bian; each was posthumously honored in turn as Grand Guardian.

sentences.zh: 建立少鷙猛無檢。

translations.literal: Jianli in youth was fierce and unrestrained.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Jianli was fierce and unrestrained.

sentences.zh: 明宗領代州刺史，擢為虞候將。

translations.literal: When Mingzong held the post of prefect of Daizhou, he was promoted to garrison duty officer.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong was prefect of Daizhou, he promoted Jianli to garrison duty officer.

sentences.zh: 莊宗鎮晉陽，以諸陵在代郡，遣女使饗祭，其下有擾於民者，建立必捕而笞之。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong was stationed at Jinyang, because the imperial tombs were in Daizhou he sent palace women to offer sacrifices; whenever any of their attendants troubled the people, Jianli would always seize and flog them.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong was stationed at Jinyang, he sent palace women to offer sacrifices at the tombs in Daizhou; whenever any of their attendants harassed the people, Jianli would seize and flog them.

sentences.zh: 莊宗怒，令收之，為明宗所護而免，由是知名。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong was angry and ordered him seized; Mingzong protected him and he was spared, and from this he became known.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong was furious and ordered him arrested, but Mingzong protected him and he was spared; from this he became well known.

sentences.zh: 明宗歷遷藩鎮，皆署為牙門都校，累奏加檢校司空。

translations.literal: As Mingzong moved through successive frontier commands, he was always appointed gate commander of the headquarters guard, and through repeated memorials was given the honorary title of Acting Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: As Mingzong moved from one military governorship to another, he always appointed Jianli headquarters guard commander, and through repeated recommendations he received the honorary rank of Acting Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 及明宗為魏軍所迫，時皇后曹氏、淑妃王氏在常山，使建立殺其監護並部下兵，故明宗家屬因而保全。

translations.literal: When Mingzong was pressed by the Wei army, the empress consort Cao and the honored consort Wang were at Changshan; he had Jianli kill their guards and the troops under them, and thus Mingzong's family was preserved.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong was driven by the Wei army, Empress Cao and Honored Consort Wang were at Changshan; he had Jianli kill their guards and escort troops, and so Mingzong's family was saved.

sentences.zh: 及即位，以功授鎮州節度副使，加檢校司徒，旋為留後。

translations.literal: When Mingzong took the throne, for his merit he was made deputy military governor of Zhenzhou and given Acting Minister over the Masses, and soon became acting governor.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong took the throne, Jianli was made deputy military governor of Zhenzhou for his service and given the honorary rank of Acting Minister over the Masses, and soon became acting governor.

sentences.zh: 未幾，正授節旄，繼加檢校太尉、同平章事。

translations.literal: Before long he received the full commission as military governor and was further given Acting Grand Commandant and co–Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he received full appointment as military governor and was further given Acting Grand Commandant and co–Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 會王都據中山叛，密使通弟兄之好。

translations.literal: When Wang Du held Zhongshan in rebellion, he secretly sent envoys to pledge brotherly friendship.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Du rebelled and held Zhongshan, he secretly sent envoys to propose a brotherly alliance.

sentences.zh: （《通鑒》：王都陰與謀復河北故事，建立陽許而密奏之。）〉

translations.literal: (From the 《Zizhi Tongjian》: Wang Du secretly plotted to restore the old Hebei arrangement; Jianli agreed openly but memorialized the court in secret.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (According to the 《Zizhi Tongjian》, Wang Du secretly plotted to restore the old Hebei autonomy; Jianli agreed openly but reported him secretly to the court.)〉

sentences.zh: 安重誨素與建立不協，知其事，奏之。

translations.literal: An Chonghui had long been at odds with Jianli; learning of the affair, he memorialized it.
translations.idiomatic: An Chonghui had long been on bad terms with Jianli; when he learned of the plot, he reported it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 明宗慮陷建立，尋征赴闕，

translations.literal: Mingzong feared Jianli would be trapped and soon summoned him to court,
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Jianli would be implicated, Mingzong soon summoned him to court,

sentences.zh: （《通鑒》：建立奏重誨專權，求入朝面言其狀，帝召之。）〉

translations.literal: (From the 《Zizhi Tongjian》: Jianli memorialized that Chonghui monopolized power and asked to enter court in person to state the facts; the emperor summoned him.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (According to the 《Zizhi Tongjian》, Jianli memorialized that Chonghui was abusing his power and asked to come to court in person to state his case; the emperor summoned him.)〉

sentences.zh: 拜右僕射兼中書侍郎、平章事、判鹽鐵戶部度支，充集賢殿大學士。

translations.literal: He was appointed Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, concurrent Vice Director of the Secretariat, Grand Councillor, controller of salt, iron, revenue, and expenditure, and Grand Academician of the Hall for Gathering Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, Vice Director of the Secretariat, Grand Councillor, controller of salt, iron, and fiscal affairs, and Grand Academician of the Hall for Gathering Worthies.

sentences.zh: 天成四年，出為青州節度使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tiancheng he was sent out as military governor of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Tiancheng (929) he was sent out as military governor of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 五年，移鎮上黨，辭不赴任，請退居丘園，制以太子少保致仕，建立自是郁郁不得志。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was transferred to govern Shangdang; he declined the appointment and asked to retire to his home district; an edict made him Retired Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and from then on Jianli was depressed and unfulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was transferred to Shangdang; he declined the post and asked to retire to his home; he was made Retired Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and from then on lived in frustrated obscurity.

sentences.zh: 長興中，嘗欲求見，中旨不許，皆重誨蔽之也。

translations.literal: In the Changxing era he once sought an audience; the imperial order did not permit it—all because Chonghui blocked him.
translations.idiomatic: During Changxing he once sought an audience with the emperor, but the court refused—Chonghui had blocked him.

sentences.zh: 清泰初，末帝召赴闕，授天平軍節度使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qingtai the Last Emperor summoned him to court and made him military governor of the Tianping Army.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Qingtai the Last Emperor summoned him to court and appointed him military governor of the Tianping Army.

sentences.zh: 建立少歷軍校，職當捕盜，及位居方伯，為政嚴烈。

translations.literal: Jianli in youth had served as army officer with duty to catch bandits; when he reached the rank of regional lord his governance was severe and fierce.
translations.idiomatic: Jianli had begun as an army officer whose duty was to catch bandits; once he became a regional governor his rule was harsh and severe.

sentences.zh: 閭裏有惡跡者，必族而誅之，其刑失於入者，不可勝紀，故當時人目之為「王垛疊」，言殺其人而積其屍也。

translations.literal: Whenever there were evildoers in the villages he would exterminate the whole clan; cases in which punishment fell on the innocent were beyond counting, so people of the time called him "Wang the Stacker," meaning he killed people and piled up their corpses.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever evildoers appeared in the villages he would exterminate entire clans; innocent people punished were beyond counting, and contemporaries called him "Wang the Stacker"—meaning he killed men and heaped up their corpses.

sentences.zh: 後聞末帝失勢，殺副使李彥赟及從事一人，報其私怨，人甚鄙之。

translations.literal: Later, hearing that the Last Emperor had lost power, he killed Deputy Commissioner Li Yanyun and one staff member to settle private grudges; people despised him greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Later, hearing that the Last Emperor had lost power, he killed Deputy Commissioner Li Yanyun and one staff member to settle old scores; people despised him for it.

sentences.zh: 高祖即位，再為青州節度使，累加檢校太尉、兼中書令。

translations.literal: When the High Ancestor took the throne, he again became military governor of Qingzhou and was repeatedly given Acting Grand Commandant and concurrent Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When the High Ancestor took the throne, Jianli was again made military governor of Qingzhou and was given Acting Grand Commandant and concurrent Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 建立晚年，歸心釋氏，飯僧營寺，戒殺慎獄，民稍安之。

translations.literal: In his later years Jianli turned his heart to Buddhism, fed monks and built temples, forbade killing and was cautious in prisons, and the people were somewhat reassured.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years Jianli turned to Buddhism, fed monks and built temples, forbade killing and was careful in administering justice, and the people were somewhat reassured.

sentences.zh: 天福二年，封臨淄王。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianfu he was enfeoffed as Prince of Linzi.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianfu (937) he was enfeoffed as Prince of Linzi.

sentences.zh: 明年，封東平王。

translations.literal: The next year he was enfeoffed as Prince of Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was enfeoffed as Prince of Dongping.

sentences.zh: 五年，入覲，高祖曰：「三紀前老兄，宜賜不拜。」

translations.literal: In the fifth year he came to court for an audience; the High Ancestor said: "An elder brother from three generations ago—you should be granted exemption from bowing."
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he came to court; the High Ancestor said, "An elder brother from three generations past—you should be excused from bowing."

sentences.zh: 仍許肩輿入朝，上殿則使二宦者掖之，論者榮之。

translations.literal: He was also permitted to enter court in a shoulder-borne carriage; when he ascended the hall two eunuchs supported him—commentators honored this.
translations.idiomatic: He was also allowed to enter court in a sedan chair, and when he ascended the hall two eunuchs supported him—onlookers regarded this as a great honor.

sentences.zh: 尋表乞休致，高祖不允。

translations.literal: Soon he memorialized asking to retire; the High Ancestor did not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: He soon memorialized asking to retire, but the High Ancestor refused.

sentences.zh: 乃授潞州節度使，割遼、沁二州為上黨屬郡，加檢校太師，進封韓王，以光其故裏。

translations.literal: He was then made military governor of Luzhou; Liao and Qin prefectures were cut off as subordinate commanderies of Shangdang; he was given Acting Grand Preceptor and advanced to Prince of Han to glorify his native place.
translations.idiomatic: He was then appointed military governor of Luzhou; Liao and Qin were detached as subordinate prefectures of Shangdang; he was given Acting Grand Preceptor and advanced to Prince of Han to honor his homeland.

sentences.zh: 至鎮逾月而疾作，有大星墜於府署，建立即召賓介竺嶽草遺章，又謂其子守恩曰：「榆社之地，桑梓存焉，桑以養生，梓以送死。

translations.literal: More than a month after reaching his post illness came on; a great star fell in the government compound; Jianli immediately summoned his staff member Zhu Yue to draft his final memorial and said to his son Shou'en: "In the land of Yushe our native roots remain—mulberry to sustain life, catalpa to send off the dead.
translations.idiomatic: A little over a month after reaching his post he fell ill; a great star fell in the government compound; Jianli at once had his staff member Zhu Yue draft his final memorial and said to his son Shou'en: "In Yushe our ancestral land remains—mulberry to sustain life, catalpa to lay out the dead.

sentences.zh: 余生為壽宮，刻銘石室，死當速葬，葬必從儉，違吾是言，非孝也。」

translations.literal: In life I have made a longevity palace and inscribed a stone chamber; when I die you must bury me quickly, and the burial must be frugal—whoever violates these words of mine is not filial."
translations.idiomatic: In life I have built a tomb and carved an inscription in stone; when I die bury me quickly, and let the burial be simple—whoever disobeys these words is not filial."

sentences.zh: 旋以病篤而卒，年七十。

translations.literal: Soon, as his illness grew grave, he died at the age of seventy.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died of his illness at the age of seventy.

sentences.zh: 冊贈尚書令。

translations.literal: By patent he was posthumously made Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 建立先人之墳在於榆社，其崗阜重復，松檜藹然，占者云「後必出公侯」，故建立自為墓，恐子孫易之也。

translations.literal: The tomb of Jianli's forebears was at Yushe; its mounds rose in layers and pines and cypresses grew luxuriantly; diviners said "later there will surely come dukes and marquises," so Jianli made his own tomb himself, fearing his descendants might change it.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestors were buried at Yushe on layered hills covered with pines and cypresses; diviners had said that dukes and marquises would surely come from that line, so Jianli built his own tomb there, fearing his descendants might move it.

sentences.zh: 子守恩，《周書》有傳。

translations.literal: His son Shou'en has a biography in the 《Book of Zhou》.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shou'en has a biography in the 《Book of Zhou》.

sentences.zh: 康福，蔚州人，世為本州軍校。

translations.literal: Kang Fu was a man of Weizhou; for generations his family had been army officers of that prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Fu was from Weizhou; for generations his family had served as army officers of that prefecture.

sentences.zh: 祖嗣，蕃漢都知兵馬使，累贈太子太師。

translations.literal: His grandfather Si was overall tribal-and-Han commander of troops and horses and was posthumously honored in succession as Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Si had been overall commander of tribal and Han troops and horses and was posthumously honored as Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 父公政，歷職至平塞軍使，累贈太傅。

translations.literal: His father Gongzheng rose in office to commander of the Pingsai Army and was posthumously honored in succession as Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: His father Gongzheng rose to commander of the Pingsai Army and was posthumously honored as Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 福便弓馬，少事後唐武皇，累補軍職，充承天軍都監。

translations.literal: Fu was skilled with bow and horse; in youth he served the Martial Emperor of Later Tang and was repeatedly appointed to army posts, serving as overall supervisor of the Chengtian Army.
translations.idiomatic: Fu was skilled with bow and horse; in youth he served the Martial Emperor of Later Tang, rose through army posts, and became overall supervisor of the Chengtian Army.

sentences.zh: 莊宗嗣位，嘗謂左右曰：「我本蕃人，以羊馬為活業。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong succeeded to the throne he once said to those at his side: "I am originally a tribesman; sheep and horses are my livelihood.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong succeeded to the throne he once told his attendants, "I am a tribesman by origin; sheep and horses are how I make my living.

sentences.zh: 彼康福者，體貌豐厚，宜領財貨，可令總轄馬牧。」

translations.literal: That Kang Fu has a full and substantial physique and is fit to oversee wealth and goods—he may be ordered to take overall charge of horse pastures.
translations.idiomatic: That Kang Fu has a stout build and is fit to manage wealth—let him take charge of the horse pastures.

sentences.zh: 由是署為馬坊使，大有蕃息。

translations.literal: From this he was appointed horse-pasture commissioner and greatly increased the herds.
translations.idiomatic: He was accordingly appointed horse-pasture commissioner, and the herds flourished greatly.

sentences.zh: 及明宗為亂兵所迫，將離魏縣，會福牧小坊馬數千匹於相州，乃驅而歸。

translations.literal: When Mingzong was pressed by mutinous troops and was about to leave Weixian, Fu happened to be pasturing several thousand horses of the minor pastures at Xiangzhou and drove them back with him.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong was driven by mutinous troops and was about to leave Weixian, Fu happened to be pasturing several thousand horses from the minor pastures at Xiangzhou and drove them back with him.

sentences.zh: 明宗即位，授飛龍使，俄轉磁州刺史，充襄州兵馬都監。

translations.literal: When Mingzong took the throne he was made Flying Dragon Commissioner; soon he was transferred to prefect of Cizhou and made overall supervisor of troops and horses at Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong took the throne he was made Flying Dragon Commissioner; soon he became prefect of Cizhou and overall supervisor of troops and horses at Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 尋以江陵叛命，朝廷舉兵伐之，以福為荊南道行營兵馬都監，俄以王師無功而還。

translations.literal: Soon, because Jiangling rebelled against orders, the court raised troops against it and made Fu overall supervisor of troops and horses for the Jingnan campaign headquarters; before long the imperial army returned without success.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Jiangling rebelled; the court marched against it and made Fu overall supervisor of troops and horses for the Jingnan campaign; the imperial army soon returned without success.

sentences.zh: 福善諸蕃語，明宗視政之暇，每召入便殿，諮訪時之利病，福即以蕃語奏之。

translations.literal: Fu was skilled in various tribal languages; in Mingzong's leisure from attending to government he would summon him into the private hall and consult on the advantages and harms of the times; Fu would report in tribal language.
translations.idiomatic: Fu was skilled in several tribal languages; in his leisure from government Mingzong would summon him to the private hall to ask about current affairs, and Fu would answer in his native tongue.

sentences.zh: 樞密使重誨惡焉，常面戒之曰：「康福但亂奏事，有日斬之！」

translations.literal: The Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs Chonghui hated this and often warned him to his face: "Kang Fu only muddles memorials—one day he will be beheaded!"
translations.idiomatic: Chief Councillor Chonghui hated this and often warned him to his face: "Kang Fu only muddles affairs at court—one day I'll have him beheaded!"

sentences.zh: 福懼。

translations.literal: Fu was afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Fu was terrified.

sentences.zh: 會靈武兵馬留後韓潯，以人情不協，慮為所圖，上表請帥，制加福光祿大夫、檢校司空，行涼州刺史，充朔方、河西等軍節度，靈威雄警甘肅等州觀察處置、管內營田、押蕃落、溫池榷稅等使。

translations.literal: When Han Xun, acting commander of troops and horses at Lingwu, because popular sentiment was not harmonious feared he would be plotted against and memorialized asking for a commander, an edict gave Fu the title of Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Acting Minister of Works, acting prefect of Liangzhou, military governor of the Shuofang and Hexi armies, observer and administrator of Ling, Wei, Xiong, Jing, Gan, and Su prefectures, director of garrison farming within the circuit, commissioner for tribal peoples, and commissioner for the salt monopoly at Wench Pool.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Xun, acting commander at Lingwu, feared conspiracy because he was unpopular with his troops and asked for a new commander, Fu was given the titles of Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Acting Minister of Works, made acting prefect of Liangzhou and military governor of Shuofang and Hexi, and placed in charge of observation and administration over Ling, Wei, Xiong, Jing, Gan, and Su, garrison farming, tribal affairs, and the salt monopoly at Wench Pool.

sentences.zh: 福之是拜，蓋重誨嫉而出之，福泣而辭之。

translations.literal: Fu's receiving this appointment was because Chonghui envied him and sent him out; Fu wept as he declined it.
translations.idiomatic: Fu received this appointment because Chonghui envied him and wanted him out of court; Fu wept as he tried to decline.

sentences.zh: 明宗宣重誨別與商議，重誨奏曰：「臣累奉聖旨，令與康福一事，今福驟升節鎮，更欲何求！

translations.literal: Mingzong had Chonghui discuss it separately; Chonghui memorialized: "Your servant has repeatedly received the sacred order to settle one matter with Kang Fu; now Fu has suddenly risen to a frontier command—what more does he want!
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong had Chonghui discuss the matter separately; Chonghui memorialized, "I have repeatedly received Your Majesty's order to settle affairs with Kang Fu; now he has suddenly been made a frontier governor—what more could he want!

sentences.zh: 況已有成命，難於改移。」

translations.literal: Moreover the appointment is already settled and hard to change."
translations.idiomatic: Besides, the appointment has already been issued and cannot easily be changed."

sentences.zh: 明宗不得已，謂福曰：「重誨不肯，非朕意也。」

translations.literal: Mingzong had no choice and said to Fu: "Chonghui will not agree—this is not my intent."
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong had no choice and told Fu, "Chonghui will not agree—this is not what I want."

sentences.zh: 福辭，明宗曰：「朕遣兵援助，勿過憂也。」

translations.literal: Fu declined further concern, and Mingzong said, "I will send troops to aid you—do not worry overmuch."
translations.idiomatic: Fu thanked him, and Mingzong said, "I will dispatch troops to support you; do not worry too much."

sentences.zh: 因令將軍牛知柔領兵送赴鎮。

translations.literal: He then ordered General Niu Zhirou to lead troops and escort him to his command.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered General Niu Zhirou to lead troops and escort Fu to his post.

sentences.zh: 行次青崗峽，會大雪，令人登山望之，見川下煙火，吐蕃數千帳在焉，寇不之覺，因分軍三道以掩之。

translations.literal: On the march they reached Qinggang Gorge; heavy snow fell, and he had men climb the mountain to look out. They saw smoke and fire below in the valley—several thousand Tibetan tents were there. The enemy did not notice them, so he divided his army into three routes to surprise them.
translations.idiomatic: En route they reached Qinggang Gorge during a heavy snowfall. Fu sent men up the heights to scout and spotted smoke and fires in the valley below—several thousand Tibetan tents lay there, unaware of his approach. He split his force into three columns and fell upon them.

sentences.zh: 蕃眾大駭，棄帳幕而走，殺之殆盡，獲玉璞、羊馬甚多。

translations.literal: The tribal masses were greatly terrified, abandoned their tents and fled, and were nearly all killed; very many jade pieces, sheep, and horses were captured.
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetans panicked, abandoned their tents, and fled; nearly all were killed, and a great haul of jade, sheep, and horses was taken.

sentences.zh: 到鎮歲餘，西戎皆款附，改賜福耀忠匡定保節功臣，累加官爵。

translations.literal: After more than a year at his post, the western tribes all submitted in good faith; Fu was re-granted the title Meritorious Minister of Glorious Loyalty, Rectification, Stabilization, and Preservation of Integrity, and his offices and ranks were repeatedly raised.
translations.idiomatic: After he had been at his post for more than a year, the western tribes all came peacefully to terms. Fu was given the honorary title Meritorious Minister of Glorious Loyalty, Rectification, Stabilization, and Preservation of Integrity, and his offices and ranks were raised again and again.

sentences.zh: 福鎮靈武凡三歲，每歲大稔，倉儲盈羨，有馬千駟，因為人所譖。

translations.literal: Fu governed Lingwu for three years in all; each year brought a great harvest, the granaries overflowed with surplus, and he had a thousand teams of horses—whereupon he was slandered by others.
translations.idiomatic: Fu governed Lingwu for three years altogether. Each year brought abundant harvests, the storehouses brimmed with surplus grain, and he possessed a thousand teams of horses—until men began to slander him.

sentences.zh: 安重誨奏曰：「累據使臣所言，康福大有寶貨，必負朝廷。」

translations.literal: An Chonghui memorialized, saying, "According repeatedly to what envoys report, Kang Fu possesses great treasure and goods and must be disloyal to the court."
translations.idiomatic: An Chonghui memorialized, "Envoys have repeatedly reported that Kang Fu has amassed great wealth and must be disloyal to the court."

sentences.zh: 明宗密遣人謂曰：「朕何負於卿，而有異心耶！」

translations.literal: Mingzong secretly sent someone to tell him, "How have I wronged you, that you should harbor a different heart!"
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong secretly sent a messenger to ask him, "What have I done to wrong you, that you would turn disloyal?"

sentences.zh: 福奏曰：「臣受國重恩，有死無貳，豈願負於聖人，此必讒人之言也。」

translations.literal: Fu memorialized, saying, "Your servant has received the state's heavy grace; I would die rather than be disloyal—how could I wish to wrong the sage ruler? This must be the words of slanderers."
translations.idiomatic: Fu replied in a memorial, "I have received the deepest favor from the state and would die before being disloyal. How could I ever betray Your Majesty? This must be the talk of slanderers."

sentences.zh: 因表乞入覲，不允。

translations.literal: He then submitted a memorial requesting an audience at court; it was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: He then petitioned for permission to come to court, but the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 及再上章，隨而赴闕，移授彰義軍節度使，又轉邠州，檢校太傅。

translations.literal: When he submitted another memorial, he proceeded at once to the capital; he was transferred and appointed military governor of the Zhangyi Army, then moved to Binzhou as honorary Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: When he submitted a second memorial, he went straight to the capital. He was reassigned as military governor of the Zhangyi Army, then transferred to Binzhou with the honorary title Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 清泰中，移鎮秦州，加特進、開國侯，充西面都部署。

translations.literal: During Qingtai he was transferred to govern Qinzhou, given the rank of Special Advancement and Marquis Who Establishes the State, and made overall commander of the western frontier.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qingtai era he was transferred to Qinzhou, granted Special Advancement and the title Marquis Who Establishes the State, and appointed overall commander of the western frontier.

sentences.zh: 高祖受命，就加檢校太尉、開國公。

translations.literal: When Gaozu received the Mandate, Fu was thereupon additionally made honorary Grand Marshal and Duke Who Establishes the State.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne, Fu was at once promoted to honorary Grand Marshal and Duke Who Establishes the State.

sentences.zh: 未幾，又加同平章事。

translations.literal: Before long he was additionally made Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was also made Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 及移領河中，加兼侍中。

translations.literal: When he was transferred to take charge of Hezhong, he was additionally made concurrent Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When he was transferred to govern Hezhong, he was also made concurrent Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 以天和節入覲，改賜輸忠守正翊亮功臣，加開府儀同三司，增食邑至五千戶，實封五百戶。

translations.literal: On the Tianhe festival he entered court for an audience; he was re-granted the title Meritorious Minister of Loyal Service, Upright Conduct, and Assisting Brilliance, made Grand Master of Splendid Honors with Grand Precedence, and his fief was increased to five thousand households with five hundred actually enfeoffed.
translations.idiomatic: He came to court for an audience on the Tianhe festival and was given the honorary title Meritorious Minister of Loyal Service, Upright Conduct, and Assisting Brilliance, along with the rank of Grand Master of Splendid Honors with Grand Precedence. His nominal fief was raised to five thousand households, with five hundred actually enfeoffed.

sentences.zh: 久之，受代歸闕。

translations.literal: After a long time he was replaced and returned to court.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was relieved of his post and returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 天福七年秋，卒於京師，年五十八。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the seventh year of Tianfu he died in the capital at the age of fifty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the seventh year of Tianfu (942) he died in the capital at the age of fifty-eight.

sentences.zh: 贈太師，謚曰武安。

translations.literal: He was posthumously honored as Grand Preceptor, with the posthumous name Wu'an.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Grand Preceptor and given the posthumous name Wu'an.

sentences.zh: 福無軍功，屬明宗龍躍，有際會之幸，擢自小校，暴為貴人，每食非羊之全髀不能飫腹，與士大夫交言，懵無所別。

translations.literal: Fu had no military achievement; when Mingzong rose like a dragon he had the good fortune of timely opportunity, was promoted from a minor officer, and suddenly became a person of rank. At each meal he could not fill his belly unless he had a whole sheep's hind leg; in conversing with scholar-officials he was ignorant and made no distinctions.
translations.idiomatic: Fu had won no military distinction. When Mingzong seized the throne he happened to be in the right place at the right time, rising from a lowly officer to sudden eminence. He would not consider a meal complete unless it included an entire mutton leg, and in conversation with scholar-officials he was utterly uncouth and undiscriminating.

sentences.zh: 在天水日，嘗有疾，幕客謁問，福擁衾而坐。

translations.literal: On the days when he was at Tianshui he once fell ill; staff guests came to inquire after him, and Fu sat wrapped in his quilt.
translations.idiomatic: While he was at Tianshui he once fell ill. His staff came to inquire after him and found Fu sitting up wrapped in his bedding.

sentences.zh: 客有退者，謂同列曰：「錦衾爛兮！」

translations.literal: One guest who withdrew said to his colleagues, "The brocade quilt—how splendid!"
translations.idiomatic: As one guest withdrew, he remarked to his colleagues, "What splendid brocade bedding!"

sentences.zh: 福聞之，遽召言者，怒視曰：「吾雖生於塞下，乃唐人也，何得以為爛奚！」

translations.literal: Fu heard this, hastily summoned the speaker, glared in anger, and said, "Although I was born beyond the frontier, I am a man of Tang—how dare you take me for a Lanxi!"
translations.idiomatic: Fu overheard him, immediately summoned the man, and glared in fury. "I may have been born on the frontier," he said, "but I am a man of Tang. How dare you call me a barbarian!"

sentences.zh: 因叱出之，由是諸客不敢措辭。

translations.literal: He then shouted and drove him out; from this all the guests dared not put words together.
translations.idiomatic: He then berated the man and had him thrown out. After that none of his guests dared speak freely.

sentences.zh: 復有末客姓駱，其先與後唐懿祖來自金山府，因公宴，福謂從事輩曰：「駱評事官則卑，門族甚高，真沙陀也。」

translations.literal: There was also a junior guest surnamed Luo, whose forebears had come from Jinshan Prefecture with Later Tang's Honored Ancestor; at a public banquet Fu said to his staff officers, "Reviewer Luo's office is low, but his clan is very eminent—he is truly Shatuo."
translations.idiomatic: There was also a junior guest named Luo whose ancestors had come from Jinshan Prefecture with Later Tang's Honored Ancestor. At a banquet Fu told his staff, "Reviewer Luo may hold a low post, but his family is very distinguished—he is true Shatuo stock."

sentences.zh: 聞者竊笑焉。

translations.literal: Those who heard it secretly laughed.
translations.idiomatic: Those who heard him quietly laughed to themselves.

sentences.zh: 子三人：長曰延沼，歷隨、澤二州刺史；

translations.literal: He had three sons: the eldest was named Yanzhao, who served successively as prefect of Sui and Ze;
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons. The eldest, Yanzhao, served successively as prefect of Sui and Ze;

sentences.zh: 次曰延澤、延壽，俱歷內職焉。

translations.literal: the next were named Yanze and Yanshou, both of whom served in inner-court posts.
translations.idiomatic: the next two, Yanze and Yanshou, both held posts in the inner court.

sentences.zh: 安彥威，字國俊，代州崞縣人。

translations.literal: An Yanwei, style name Guojun, was a man of Guo County in Daizhou.
translations.idiomatic: An Yanwei, whose courtesy name was Guojun, came from Guo County in Daizhou.

sentences.zh: 少時以軍卒隸唐明宗麾下，彥威善射，頗知兵法，明宗愛之。

translations.literal: In youth, as a soldier he served under Tang Mingzong; Yanwei was skilled in archery and knew military methods fairly well, and Mingzong favored him.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he served as a soldier under Tang Mingzong. Yanwei was a fine archer and knew something of military strategy, and Mingzong took a liking to him.

sentences.zh: 及領諸鎮節鉞，彥威常為牙將，以謹厚見信。

translations.literal: When Mingzong took command of the various garrison commands, Yanwei regularly served as a guard officer and was trusted for his prudence and steadiness.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Mingzong held command of a military governorship, Yanwei served as one of his guard officers and was trusted for his prudence and reliability.

sentences.zh: 明宗入立，皇子從榮鎮鄴，彥威為護聖指揮使；

translations.literal: When Mingzong entered and took the throne, the prince Congrong governed Ye, and Yanwei was Protective Sage Commander;
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong took the throne, Prince Congrong was stationed at Ye, and Yanwei served as Protective Sage Commander;

sentences.zh: 以從榮判六軍，彥威入司禁衛，遙領鎮州節度使。

translations.literal: when Congrong took charge of the Six Armies, Yanwei entered to manage the palace guard and remotely held the post of military governor of Zhenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: when Congrong took charge of the Six Armies, Yanwei entered the capital to command the palace guard and held the post of military governor of Zhenzhou in absentia.

sentences.zh: 及高祖入立，拜彥威北京留守，徙鎮歸德，是時河決滑州，命彥威塞之，彥威出私錢募民治堤。

translations.literal: When Gaozu entered and took the throne, Yanwei was appointed regent of the northern capital; he was transferred to govern Guide. At that time the Yellow River breached its banks at Huazhou, and he was ordered to stop it; Yanwei spent his private funds to recruit the people to repair the dikes.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne, Yanwei was appointed regent of the northern capital, then transferred to govern Guide. The Yellow River had breached its banks at Huazhou, and he was ordered to contain the flood. Yanwei spent his own money to hire local people to repair the dikes.

sentences.zh: 遷西京留守，遭歲大饑，彥威賑饑民，民有犯法，皆寬貸之，饑民愛之不忍去。

translations.literal: He was moved to regent of the western capital; a year of great famine struck, and Yanwei relieved the starving people. When the people broke the law he pardoned them all, and the starving people loved him and could not bear to leave.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to regent of the western capital during a year of severe famine. Yanwei fed the hungry, and when people broke the law he showed them leniency. The starving populace grew so attached to him that they could not bear to leave.

sentences.zh: 旋丁母艱，哀毀過制。

translations.literal: Soon he suffered his mother's death and mourned with grief exceeding the prescribed rites.
translations.idiomatic: He soon lost his mother and mourned her with a grief that exceeded proper ritual limits.

sentences.zh: 少帝與契丹構患，拜彥威北面行營副都統，彥威悉以家財佐軍，後以疾卒於京師。

translations.literal: When the Young Emperor came into conflict with the Khitans, Yanwei was appointed deputy overall commander of the northern campaign headquarters; Yanwei contributed his entire family wealth to support the army, and later died of illness in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When the Young Emperor came into conflict with the Khitans, Yanwei was appointed deputy overall commander of the northern campaign. He poured his entire family fortune into the war effort, but later died of illness in the capital.

sentences.zh: 彥威與太妃同宗，少帝事以為舅，彥威未嘗以為言。

translations.literal: Yanwei was of the same clan as the Consort Dowager; the Young Emperor treated him as a maternal uncle, but Yanwei never spoke of it.
translations.idiomatic: Yanwei belonged to the same clan as the Consort Dowager, and the Young Emperor treated him as a maternal uncle, but Yanwei never mentioned the connection.

sentences.zh: 及卒，太妃臨哭，人始知其為國戚，當時益重其人焉。

translations.literal: When he died the Consort Dowager came to weep at his coffin, and people first learned that he was an imperial relative; at the time this further enhanced regard for the man.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, the Consort Dowager came to mourn at his coffin, and only then did people learn he was related to the imperial house. At the time this only increased respect for him.

sentences.zh: 李周，字通理，邢州內丘人也，唐潞州節度使抱真之後。

translations.literal: Li Zhou, style name Tongli, was a man of Neiqiu in Xingzhou, a descendant of Tang's military governor of Luzhou, Baozhen.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhou, whose courtesy name was Tongli, came from Neiqiu in Xingzhou. He was a descendant of Baozhen, military governor of Luzhou under Tang.

sentences.zh: 曾祖融、祖毅、父矩，皆不仕。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Rong, grandfather Yi, and father Ju all did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Rong, grandfather Yi, and father Ju all declined official service.

sentences.zh: 周年十六，為內丘捕賊將，以任俠自負。

translations.literal: When Zhou was sixteen he was a bandit-catching officer in Neiqiu and prided himself on chivalrous daring.
translations.idiomatic: At sixteen Zhou served as a bandit-catcher in Neiqiu and prided himself on his chivalrous spirit.

sentences.zh: 時河朔群盜充斥，南北交兵，行旅無援者不敢出郡邑。

translations.literal: At the time bandits filled the Hebei region, armies clashed north and south, and travelers without escort dared not leave their districts and towns.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits swarmed across Hebei, armies clashed to north and south, and travelers without an escort dared not venture beyond their home districts.

sentences.zh: 有士人盧嶽，家於太原，攜妻子囊橐寓於逆旅，進退無所保，唯與所親相對流涕，周憫之，請援送以歸。

translations.literal: There was a scholar named Lu Yue, whose family was in Taiyuan; he brought wife, children, and baggage and lodged at an inn, with no protection whether advancing or retreating, and could only weep face to face with those close to him. Zhou pitied him and asked to escort him home.
translations.idiomatic: A scholar named Lu Yue, whose home was in Taiyuan, was traveling with his wife, children, and belongings and had taken refuge at an inn. With no safe way forward or back, he could only weep with his companions. Zhou took pity on him and offered to escort him home.

sentences.zh: 行經西山中，有賊夜於林麓間俟之，射盧嶽，中其馬。

translations.literal: Passing through the western mountains, bandits waited for them at night in the wooded foothills, shot at Lu Yue, and struck his horse.
translations.idiomatic: On the road through the western mountains, bandits lay in wait at night in the wooded foothills, shot at Lu Yue, and hit his horse.

sentences.zh: 周大呼曰：「爾為誰耶？」

translations.literal: Zhou shouted loudly, "Who are you?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhou shouted, "Who goes there?"

sentences.zh: 賊聞其聲，相謂曰：「李君至此矣。」

translations.literal: The bandits heard his voice and said to one another, "Master Li has come here."
translations.idiomatic: Hearing his voice, the bandits said to one another, "It is Master Li!"

sentences.zh: 即時散走。

translations.literal: At once they scattered and fled.
translations.idiomatic: They immediately broke and ran.

sentences.zh: 嶽全其行裝，至於家。

translations.literal: Yue kept all his traveling gear intact and reached home.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yue arrived home with all his belongings intact.

sentences.zh: 周將辭去，嶽謂周曰：「嶽明歷象，善知人。

translations.literal: When Zhou was about to take his leave, Yue said to Zhou, "Yue understands the calendar and heavenly signs and is skilled at reading people.
translations.idiomatic: As Zhou prepared to leave, Lu Yue told him, "I am versed in astronomy and skilled at reading men.

sentences.zh: 子有奇表，方頤隆準，眉目疏朗，身長七尺，此乃將相之材也。

translations.literal: You have an extraordinary countenance—square jaw, high nose, clear brows and eyes, a height of seven feet; this is the material of generals and ministers.
translations.idiomatic: You have a remarkable bearing: a broad face, a prominent nose, clear brows and eyes, and a height of seven feet. You have the makings of a general or minister.

sentences.zh: 河東李氏將有天下，子宜事之，以求富貴。」

translations.literal: The Li family of Hedong will possess the realm; you should serve them to seek wealth and rank."
translations.idiomatic: The Li of Hedong are destined to rule the realm. You should serve them and seek your fortune."

sentences.zh: 周辭以母老而歸。

translations.literal: Zhou declined on the grounds that his mother was old and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou declined, citing his aged mother, and went home.

sentences.zh: 既而梁將葛從周拔邢、洺，唐武皇麾兵南下，築壘於青山口。

translations.literal: Before long the Liang general Ge Congzhou captured Xing and Ming; Tang's Emperor Wu led troops south and built fortifications at Qingshan Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the Liang general Ge Congzhou captured Xing and Ming, and Tang's Emperor Wu marched south and built fortifications at Qingshan Pass.

sentences.zh: 周向背莫決，因思盧嶽之言，乃投青山寨將張汙落，武皇賞之，補萬勝黃頭軍使。

translations.literal: Zhou could not decide which side to join; thinking of Lu Yue's words, he went over to the Qingshan garrison commander Zhang Wuluo. Emperor Wu rewarded him and appointed him commander of the Wansheng Yellow Head Army.
translations.idiomatic: Uncertain which side to take, Zhou remembered Lu Yue's advice and joined the Qingshan garrison under Zhang Wuluo. Emperor Wu rewarded him and made him commander of the Wansheng Yellow Head Army.

sentences.zh: 武皇之平雲州，莊宗之戰柏鄉，周皆有功，遷匡霸都指揮使。

translations.literal: In Emperor Wu's pacification of Yunzhou and Zhuangzong's battle at Baixiang, Zhou had merit in both; he was promoted to Kuangba Commander.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou distinguished himself when Emperor Wu pacified Yunzhou and again at Zhuangzong's battle of Baixiang, and was promoted to Kuangba Commander.

sentences.zh: 莊宗入魏，率兵屯臨河、楊劉，所至與士伍同甘苦。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong entered Wei, Zhou led troops stationed at Linhe and Yangliu; wherever he went he shared hardship and comfort with the rank and file.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong entered Wei, Zhou garrisoned Linhe and Yangliu and everywhere shared the hardships and comforts of his soldiers.

sentences.zh: 周尤善守備，一日奔母喪，以他將代之，既出，則其城將陷，莊宗即遣追之，使墨缞從事。

translations.literal: Zhou was especially skilled in defense and preparation. One day he rushed off for his mother's funeral and another general replaced him; once he had left, the city was about to fall, and Zhuangzong at once sent men to pursue him and had him continue his duties in unbleached mourning dress.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou was especially skilled at defense. Once, when he rushed home for his mother's funeral and another officer took his place, the city nearly fell as soon as he left. Zhuangzong immediately sent men to bring him back and had him resume command while still in mourning dress.

sentences.zh: 會莊宗北征，周與寺人焦彥賓守楊劉城，

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong marched north on campaign, Zhou and the eunuch Jiao Yanbin defended Yangliu city,
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong marched north on campaign, Zhou and the eunuch Jiao Yanbin defended the city of Yangliu,

sentences.zh: （《九國誌·焦彥賓傳》：彥賓字英服，滄州清池人。

translations.literal: (From the 《Jiuguo Zhi · Biography of Jiao Yanbin》: Yanbin's style name was Yingfu; he was a man of Qingchi in Cangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: (According to the 《Jiuguo Zhi · Biography of Jiao Yanbin》, Yanbin's courtesy name was Yingfu and he came from Qingchi in Cangzhou.

sentences.zh: 少聰敏，多智略，事武皇，尤所委信。

translations.literal: In youth he was clever and keen, possessed of much strategy; he served Emperor Wu and was especially entrusted and relied upon.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was quick-witted and resourceful. He served Emperor Wu, who relied on him with special trust.

sentences.zh: 及莊宗即位，遷左監門衛將軍，充四方館使，出護邢州軍。）〉

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong took the throne, he was transferred to General of the Left Gate Guard, made envoy of the Four Directions Hall, and sent out to protect the army of Xingzhou.)〉
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong took the throne, Yanbin was promoted to General of the Left Gate Guard, appointed envoy of the Four Directions Hall, and sent out to command the forces at Xingzhou.)〉

sentences.zh: 梁將王彥章以數萬眾攻之。

translations.literal: The Liang general Wang Yanzhang attacked it with tens of thousands of men.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang general Wang Yanzhang attacked the city with an army of tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 周日夜乘城，躬當矢石，使人馳告莊宗，請百里趨程，以紓其難。

translations.literal: Zhou day and night manned the walls, personally facing arrows and stones, and sent a man galloping to inform Zhuangzong, asking him to hurry a hundred li to relieve the crisis.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou defended the walls day and night, exposing himself to arrows and stones, and sent a messenger racing to Zhuangzong to beg him to hurry a hundred li and lift the siege.

sentences.zh: 莊宗曰：「李周在內，朕何憂也！」

translations.literal: Zhuangzong said, "With Li Zhou inside, what have I to worry about!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong said, "With Li Zhou holding the city, what have I to fear!"

sentences.zh: 遂日行二舍，不廢畋獵，既至，士眾絕糧三日矣。

translations.literal: He then marched two stages a day without abandoning hunting; when he arrived, the troops and masses had been without grain for three days.
translations.idiomatic: He marched two camps a day without giving up his hunting, and when he arrived the garrison had been without food for three days.

sentences.zh: 及攻圍既解，莊宗謂周曰：「微卿九拒之勞，諸公等為梁人所擄矣。」

translations.literal: When the siege was lifted, Zhuangzong said to Zhou, "But for your labor of nine repulsions, you gentlemen would have been captured by the men of Liang."
translations.idiomatic: After the siege was lifted, Zhuangzong told Zhou, "But for your nine successful defenses, you would all have been taken by the Liang."

sentences.zh: 同光中，歷相、蔡二州刺史，及蜀平，授西川節度副使。

translations.literal: During Tongguang he served successively as prefect of Xiang and Cai; when Shu was pacified he was appointed deputy military governor of Xichuan.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tongguang era he served as prefect of Xiang and Cai in turn, and after the conquest of Shu was appointed deputy military governor of Xichuan.

sentences.zh: 天成二年春，遷遂州兩使留後，尋正授節旄，未幾，受代歸闕。

translations.literal: In the spring of the second year of Tiancheng he was transferred to regent of the two commissioners at Suizhou; soon he received the full commission as military governor, and before long he was replaced and returned to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the second year of Tiancheng (927) he became acting governor of Suizhou, soon received full appointment as military governor, and before long was relieved and returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 三年秋，出為邠州節度使，會慶州刺史竇廷琬據城拒命，周奉詔討平之。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the third year he was sent out as military governor of Binzhou; it happened that the prefect of Qingzhou, Dou Tingwan, held the city and defied orders, and Zhou received the edict to suppress and pacify him.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the third year he was sent out as military governor of Binzhou. When Qingzhou prefect Dou Tingwan seized his city and rebelled, Zhou received orders to suppress him.

sentences.zh: 長興、清泰中，歷徐、安、雍、汴四鎮，所至無苛政，人皆樂之。

translations.literal: During Changxing and Qingtai he governed the four commands of Xu, An, Yong, and Bian; wherever he went there was no harsh government, and the people all rejoiced in him.
translations.idiomatic: During the Changxing and Qingtai eras he governed Xu, An, Yong, and Bian in succession. Nowhere did he impose harsh rule, and the people everywhere welcomed him.

sentences.zh: 高祖有天下，復鎮邠州，累官至檢校太師、兼侍中。

translations.literal: When Gaozu possessed the realm, Zhou again governed Binzhou and rose through offices to honorary Grand Preceptor and concurrent Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: After Gaozu unified the realm, Zhou again governed Binzhou and rose to honorary Grand Preceptor and concurrent Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 及罷鎮赴闕，會少帝幸澶淵，以周累朝耆德，乃命為東京留守。

translations.literal: When he was relieved of his command and went to court, it happened that the Young Emperor was visiting Chanyuan; because Zhou was a venerable elder across successive reigns, he was ordered to serve as regent of the eastern capital.
translations.idiomatic: When he was relieved of his post and came to court, the Young Emperor happened to be at Chanyuan. Because Zhou was a respected elder who had served through several reigns, he was appointed regent of the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 車駕還京，授開封尹。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage returned to the capital, he was appointed governor of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned to the capital, Zhou was appointed governor of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 及遘疾，夢焚旌旗鎧甲，因自嗟嘆，上章請退，尋卒於官，時年七十四。

translations.literal: When he fell ill he dreamed of burning banners, flags, armor, and mail; he sighed in lamentation, submitted a memorial requesting retirement, and soon died in office at the age of seventy-four.
translations.idiomatic: When he fell ill he dreamed that banners, flags, armor, and mail were being burned. He sighed in dismay, submitted a memorial asking to retire, and soon died in office at the age of seventy-four.

sentences.zh: 詔贈太師，陪葬於明宗徽陵之北。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously honored him as Grand Preceptor and granted burial beside the north of Mingzong's Huiling.
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously honored him as Grand Preceptor and granted him burial north of Mingzong's Huiling.

sentences.zh: 張從訓，字德恭。

translations.literal: Zhang Congxun, style name Degong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Congxun, whose courtesy name was Degong.

sentences.zh: 本姑臧人，其先回鶻別派，隨沙陀徙居雲中，後從唐武皇家於太原，從訓遂為太原人。

translations.literal: Originally a man of Guzang, his ancestors were a separate branch of the Uyghurs who moved with the Shatuo to dwell in Yunzhong; later they followed Tang's Emperor Wu's family to Taiyuan, and Congxun thus became a man of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was originally from Guzang. His ancestors were a Uyghur offshoot who migrated with the Shatuo to Yunzhong, then followed Tang's Emperor Wu's family to Taiyuan, and Congxun thus became a native of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 祖君政，雲州長史，識蕃字，通佛理。

translations.literal: His grandfather Junzheng was chief secretary of Yunzhou, knew tribal scripts, and understood Buddhist doctrine.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Junzheng served as chief secretary of Yunzhou, knew foreign scripts, and was versed in Buddhist doctrine.

sentences.zh: 父存信，河東蕃漢馬步軍都指揮使，武皇賜姓名，眷同親嫡，前史有傳。

translations.literal: His father Cunxin was overall commander of the mixed tribal and Han cavalry and infantry of Hedong; Emperor Wu bestowed surname and given name upon him and cherished him as his own son—earlier histories have his biography.
translations.idiomatic: His father Cunxin was overall commander of the mixed tribal and Han cavalry and infantry of Hedong. Emperor Wu gave him a surname and personal name and treated him like his own son; earlier histories contain his biography.

sentences.zh: 天福中，贈太師、中書令，追封趙國公。

translations.literal: During Tianfu he was posthumously honored as Grand Preceptor and Director of the Secretariat and posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianfu era he was posthumously honored as Grand Preceptor and Director of the Secretariat and posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 從訓讀儒書，精騎射，初為散員大將，天祐中，轄沙陀數百人，屯壺關十餘歲，節度使李嗣昭委遇之。

translations.literal: Congxun read Confucian books, was skilled in mounted archery, and at first was a loose-rein major general. During Tianyou he commanded several hundred Shatuo and garrisoned Huguan for more than ten years; the military governor Li Sizhao entrusted and favored him.
translations.idiomatic: Congxun studied the Confucian classics and excelled at mounted archery. He began as a general of the loose-rein guard. During Tianyou he commanded several hundred Shatuo troops and garrisoned Huguan for more than ten years, earning the trust and favor of military governor Li Sizhao.

sentences.zh: 莊宗與梁人相拒於德勝口，征赴軍前，補充先鋒遊奕使，俄轉雲捷指揮使、檢校司空，賜名繼鸞，從諸子之行也。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong confronted the men of Liang at Desheng Pass, Congxun was summoned to the front and appointed vanguard roaming inspector; soon he was transferred to Yunjie Commander and honorary Minister of Works, and given the name Jiluan, following the pattern of the other sons.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong faced the Liang at Desheng Pass, Congxun was summoned to the front and made vanguard roaming inspector. Soon he became Yunjie Commander and honorary Minister of Works, and was given the name Jiluan, following the naming pattern of the other sons.

sentences.zh: 明宗微時，嘗在存信麾下為都押牙，與從訓有舊，及即位，授石州刺史，復舊姓名。

translations.literal: When Mingzong was in lowly circumstances he had once served under Cunxin as chief guard officer and had old ties with Congxun; when he took the throne he appointed him prefect of Shi and restored his original surname and given name.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong was still obscure he had served under Cunxin as chief guard officer and was old friends with Congxun. When Mingzong took the throne he appointed him prefect of Shi and restored his original name.

sentences.zh: 歷憲、德二州刺史。

translations.literal: He served successively as prefect of Xian and De.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as prefect of Xian and De in succession.

sentences.zh: 高祖之鎮太原也，為少帝娶從訓長女為妃。

translations.literal: When Gaozu governed Taiyuan, he took Congxun's eldest daughter as consort for the Young Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: While Gaozu was governing Taiyuan, he arranged for the Young Emperor to marry Congxun's eldest daughter.

sentences.zh: 清泰初授唐州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qingtai he was appointed prefect of Tang.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Qingtai era he was appointed prefect of Tang.

sentences.zh: 三年，高祖舉義，從訓奉唐末帝詔，征赴行在，分領鄉兵，次於團柏谷，兵敗宵遁，潛身民間。

translations.literal: In the third year Gaozu raised the righteous uprising; Congxun received the edict of Tang's Last Emperor, was summoned to the imperial camp, and took charge of local militia; he halted at Tuanbo Valley, was defeated, fled by night, and hid himself among the common people.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, when Gaozu launched his uprising, Congxun obeyed the Last Tang Emperor's summons to the imperial camp and took command of local militia. His force halted at Tuanbo Valley, was defeated, and he fled by night, hiding among the common people.

sentences.zh: 高祖入洛，有詔搜訪，月餘乃出焉，及見戚裏之故，深加軫惻。

translations.literal: When Gaozu entered Luoyang there was an edict to search for him; after more than a month he came forth, and upon seeing his old in-law ties he was deeply moved with sympathy.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu entered Luoyang an edict went out to find him. After more than a month he emerged, and when Gaozu saw his old ties as an in-law he was deeply moved with sympathy.

sentences.zh: 尋授絳州刺史、檢校太保，在任數年，天福中，卒於官，年五十二。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed prefect of Jiang and honorary Grand Guardian; he served in office several years, and during Tianfu died in office at the age of fifty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed prefect of Jiang and honorary Grand Guardian. After several years in office he died there during the Tianfu era at the age of fifty-two.

sentences.zh: 少帝以後父之故，超贈太尉。

translations.literal: Because he was the Young Emperor's father-in-law, he was posthumously promoted beyond precedent to Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Because he was the Young Emperor's father-in-law, he was posthumously promoted to Grand Marshal, an honor beyond ordinary precedent.

sentences.zh: 弟從恩仕皇朝，為右金吾衛上將軍，卒。

translations.literal: His younger brother Congen served the imperial dynasty as senior general of the Right Golden Crown Guard and died.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Congen served the dynasty as senior general of the Right Golden Crown Guard and died in office.

sentences.zh: 始繼忠母楊氏善治產，平生積財巨萬。

translations.literal: At the beginning, Jizhong's mother, Lady Yang, was skilled at managing property; throughout her life she amassed wealth in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning, Jizhong's mother, Lady Yang, was skilled at managing property and had amassed a fortune of many tens of thousands over her lifetime.

sentences.zh: 及高祖建義於太原，楊已終，繼忠舉族家於晉陽。

translations.literal: When Gaozu established the righteous enterprise at Taiyuan, Yang had already died; Jizhong moved his whole clan to make their home at Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: By the time Gaozu launched his uprising at Taiyuan, Yang had already died, and Jizhong moved his entire clan to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 時以諸軍方困，契丹援兵又至，高祖乃使人就其第，疏其復壁，取其舊積，所獲金銀紈素甚廣，至於巾屨瑣屑之物，無不取足。

translations.literal: At the time the various armies were just exhausted and Khitan reinforcements had also arrived; Gaozu then sent men to his residence, broke through the compound walls, and took his old accumulations. The gold, silver, and silk obtained were very extensive—even scarves, shoes, and trifling small things, nothing was left untaken in full.
translations.idiomatic: The armies were exhausted and Khitan reinforcements were arriving, so Gaozu sent men to Jizhong's residence, broke through the walls, and seized Yang's old hoard. They took a vast quantity of gold, silver, and silk—even scarves, shoes, and other trifles, leaving nothing behind.

sentences.zh: 高祖既濟大事，感而奇之，故車駕入洛，繼忠雖有舊恙，連領大郡，皆楊氏之力也。

translations.literal: After Gaozu had accomplished the great enterprise, he was moved and regarded it as remarkable; thus when the imperial carriage entered Luoyang, although Jizhong had old ailments, he successively governed great prefectures—all through Lady Yang's power.
translations.idiomatic: After Gaozu succeeded in his great enterprise, he was both grateful and astonished. Thus when the imperial procession entered Luoyang, Jizhong—despite chronic illness—was given one major prefecture after another, all thanks to Lady Yang's wealth.

sentences.zh: 李頃，陳州項城人，即河陽節度使、兼侍中罕之子也。

translations.literal: Li Qing was a man of Xiangcheng in Chenzhou—the son of Han, military governor of Heyang and concurrent Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qing came from Xiangcheng in Chen Prefecture. He was the son of Han, military governor of Heyang and concurrent Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 罕之，《梁書》有傳。

translations.literal: Han Zhi has a biography in the 《Liangshu》.
translations.idiomatic: A biography of Han Zhi appears in the 《Liangshu》.

sentences.zh: 唐光啟中，罕之與河南張全義為仇，交相攻擊，罕之兵敗，北投太原，武皇以澤州處之，罕之將赴任，留頃為質焉。

translations.literal: During Guangqi of Tang, Han and Zhang Quanyi of Henan were enemies and attacked one another in turn; Han's army was defeated, he fled north to Taiyuan, and Emperor Wu stationed him at Zezhou. When Han was about to take up his appointment he left Qing behind as a hostage.
translations.idiomatic: During the Guangqi era of Tang, Han became enemies with Zhang Quanyi of Henan, and the two attacked each other in turn. Han was defeated and fled north to Taiyuan, where Emperor Wu assigned him to Ze Prefecture. When Han set out to take up the post, he left Qing behind as a hostage.

sentences.zh: 時莊宗未弱冠，因與頃遊處，甚相昵狎。

translations.literal: At the time Zhuangzong had not yet reached twenty; he associated with Qing in his travels and they were very intimate.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong was not yet twenty at the time; he spent his days with Qing and they became very close.

sentences.zh: 光啟初，罕之自澤州襲據潞州，送款於梁，武皇以頃父叛，將殺之，莊宗密與駿騎，使逃出境，頃遂奔河南。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangqi, Han Zhi seized Luzhou from Zezhou and submitted to Liang; the Martial Emperor, because Qing's father had rebelled, was about to kill him, but Zhuangzong secretly gave him fine horses and had him flee across the border; Qing then fled to Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Guangqi era Han Zhi seized Luzhou from his base in Zezhou and submitted to the Liang; because Qing's father had defected, Emperor Wu was about to execute him, but Zhuangzong secretly gave him swift horses and helped him escape the territory, and Qing fled to the Liang domains.

sentences.zh: 梁祖以其父子歸己，委遇甚厚。

translations.literal: The Liang founder regarded father and son as having come over to him and entrusted and favored them greatly.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang founder treated father and son as men who had come over to his side and favored them generously.

sentences.zh: 天復中，梁祖自鳳翔送唐昭宗歸長安，留軍萬人，命侄友倫與頃總之，以宿衛為名。

translations.literal: In the Tianfu era the Liang founder escorted Tang Emperor Zhaozong from Fengxiang back to Chang'an, left ten thousand troops, and ordered his nephew Youlun and Qing to command them under the name of palace guard duty.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianfu era the Liang founder escorted Emperor Zhaozong from Fengxiang back to Chang'an, left ten thousand troops behind, and put his nephew Youlun and Qing in overall command on the pretext of palace guard duty.

sentences.zh: 及梁祖逼禪，累掌禁兵，倚為肘腋。

translations.literal: When the Liang founder forced the abdication, Qing repeatedly held command of the forbidden troops and was relied on as a close confidant.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liang founder forced the Tang abdication, Qing repeatedly commanded the palace armies and was trusted as a close confidant.

sentences.zh: 庶人友珪立，授頃檢校尚書右僕射、右羽林統軍。

translations.literal: When the commoner Yougui took the throne, Qing was made Acting Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat and commander of the Right Forest of Feathers Army.
translations.idiomatic: When the deposed emperor Yougui seized power, Qing was made Acting Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat and commander of the Right Forest of Feathers Army.

sentences.zh: 梁末帝之誅友珪，頃預其謀，尋歷隨州刺史，復為右羽林統軍。

translations.literal: When the Last Liang Emperor executed Yougui, Qing took part in the plot; soon he served as prefect of Suizhou and again became commander of the Right Forest of Feathers Army.
translations.idiomatic: When the Last Liang Emperor killed Yougui, Qing took part in the conspiracy; he soon served as prefect of Suizhou and again became commander of the Right Forest of Feathers Army.

sentences.zh: 同光初，莊宗入汴，召頃見之，莊宗忻然，授衛州刺史，加光祿大夫、檢校太保。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tongguang, Zhuangzong entered Bian and summoned Qing to see him; Zhuangzong was pleased and made him prefect of Weizhou, adding Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Acting Grand Guardian.
